diagnostic_evidence.quote: where we always take the diffusion matrix $\sigma$ equal to zero.

issues.failure_explanation: The model framework requires ΣΣ^T to be positive definite, but the numerical experiments set σ=0, making ΣΣ^T the zero matrix and outside the stated hypothesis.

failure_location.quote: definite symmetric $2\times2$ matrix and $\sigma$ denotes the volatility matrix.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'positive definite' by 'positive semidefinite' or explicitly treat the zero-diffusion case as a limiting pure-jump case.
issues.overall_effect: The stated market-model assumptions do not cover the pure-jump experimental setup; the scope of the method as described is incompatible with the experiments.
issues.title: Positive-definite diffusion assumption incompatible with zero-diffusion experiments
issues.why_classification: A one-word hypothesis correction preserves the method and all experiments; no new construction or proof is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The process X includes a Wiener term. Brownian motion has infinite path variation, so if Σ is nonzero the full process is not finite-variation even when the Lévy measure satisfies A_ell<1; only the jump component is.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the statement as 'the jump component is of finite variation' or impose Σ=0 when claiming X is finite-variation.
issues.overall_effect: The characterization and the finite-variation regime invoked for convergence refer to the jump part, not the full process; as written it is false for diffusive exponential Lévy models.
issues.title: Finite-variation statement ignores the Brownian part
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and does not alter the numerical method or the finite-variation jump regime under which the experiments are performed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: provides a necessary condition of it.

issues.failure_explanation: Finite k-th moments of the exponential asset require one-sided exponential moments of the jump component, not integrability of e^{k||z||} with respect to the Lévy density. Under the paper's own NTS tail, B_ell is the minimal norm exponential rate, so k<B_ell is sufficient, not necessary; e.g. the VG0 parameters give B_ell<2 while the process still has finite variance.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State B_ell>2 as a sufficient tail condition or replace the moment/necessity claim with the correct directional exponential-moment condition.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised hypothesis is overstrong and incorrectly characterized as necessary, excluding valid parameter sets (including VG0 used in the experiments) from the stated assumptions.
issues.title: B_ell>=2 is misstated as necessary for finite moments/finite variance
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local correction of a scope statement; it does not change the numerical construction or require a new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The text says the first time step is replaced by four θ=1 substeps of size h_t/4, but the labelled algorithm precomputes θ=1/2 and loops uniformly for n=1,...,N_t without a special first-step case or modified time step.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a special n=1 branch using four substeps with θ=1 and h_t/4 (and the corresponding ILU factorization), or remove the damping claim from the algorithm description.
issues.overall_effect: The labelled procedure does not implement the described damping for nonsmooth payoffs; the 'complete algorithm' is incomplete relative to the stated method.
issues.title: Algorithm omits the stated first-time-step damping
issues.why_classification: The omission is a local missing implementation detail; adding the described special case restores the stated algorithm without changing the main scheme architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: For d=2 and a=α,b=0, the appendix formula δΦ gives prefactor δ c1^{α+1}/(π√detρ), whereas the displayed experimental formula has δ/π·√(c1^{1+α}/detρ); these differ by a factor c1^{α+1}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the displayed density to match δΦ(x|α,0), i.e. use c1^{α+1}/(π√detρ); if the printed formula was used in the computations, recompute the experimental results.
issues.overall_effect: The Lévy measure defined for the NTS experiments is false as written, so the quadrature weights and the operators B_ω and r_ω constructed from it are unreliable for the described numerical experiments.
issues.title: Incorrect prefactor in the explicit NTS Lévy density
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and the correct formula is present in the appendix, but it changes the input measure for the entire experimental construction, so the reported numerical results cannot be taken as established without revalidation; this is more than a pure typo but does not require new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Since B(G)=ηG+√ρ W(G), Cov(L)=ρ E[G]+ηη^T Var(G). The printed formula uses ρ δΓ(2-α)λ^{1-α}/λ^{2-α} instead of ρ δΓ(1-α)/λ^{1-α}; the coefficients differ by a factor (1-α) for α>0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the formula by t[δΓ(1-α)/λ^{1-α} ρ + δΓ(2-α)/λ^{2-α} ηη^T] (or the equivalent factored form with 1/(1-α) multiplying ρ).
issues.overall_effect: The stated variance/covariance of the NTS jump process is false, and it is inconsistent with the paper's own standard-deviation/correlation table, making the parameter description unreliable.
issues.title: NTS covariance formula has wrong Brownian coefficient
issues.why_classification: A one-line formula correction fixes the stated covariance; the main pricing method and numerical scheme do not depend on this display except for interpreting the parameter table.
